gaps.title: No captured screen or flow for managers to approve or decline
gaps.description: REQ-002 (approved) has line managers approving or declining loan requests, and DEC-001 limits this to the requester's direct reports. None of the captured screens, components or flows shows where a manager finds pending requests from their reports, sees request details, or records approve or decline. Both captured screens are staff-facing (My equipment loans, Request equipment). The manager side is not shown in the capture.
gaps.why_it_matters: Approval is the step that moves a loan out of 'Requested'. Without a defined manager entry point and decision step, the core workflow of this feature cannot be specified past submission.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: The spec cannot describe how requests reach managers or how decisions are recorded, so the approval workflow could be built inconsistently or left out.

gaps.title: Outcome of submitting a request is undefined
gaps.description: The Submit request button on the Request equipment form has no target (type=button, no link or form action). The capture shows no confirmation, error state or return to the loans list, so what a staff member sees after submitting, and how the new request appears in My equipment loans, is not shown.
gaps.why_it_matters: Submitting a request is the only staff action in the mockup and it ends in a dead end. The link between REQ-001 (request) and REQ-003 (see status) depends on what happens after submit.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Staff may not know whether a request went through, and may resubmit or abandon it. The success and failure behaviour cannot be specified or tested.
research_questions: What post-submission feedback patterns do established design systems (for example GOV.UK Design System confirmation pages, or success notifications) recommend for request-style forms?
How should a successful or failed form submission be announced to assistive technology under WCAG 2.2 SC 4.1.3 Status Messages?

gaps.title: Loan status set and transitions are not defined
gaps.description: The mockup shows only the status 'Requested'. REQ-003 needs staff to see status, and REQ-002 implies approved and declined outcomes. CQ-005 (which statuses exist and what staff see beyond the status) has not been answered. What moves a loan between statuses (for example collection, return, cancellation, overdue) is not stated or shown.
gaps.why_it_matters: The Status column is the main way staff track their loans under REQ-003. The table's 'From/To' columns suggest loans have a life after approval, but no status covers that.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: REQ-003 cannot be specified, statuses may be invented during build, and staff may see wording that does not match the real process.

gaps.title: Decline reason and unactioned requests still open
gaps.description: DEC-002 settled that staff are emailed when a request is approved or declined. It did not answer the rest of CQ-004: whether a manager must give a reason when declining, whether staff can see that reason in the loans list, and what happens to a request a manager never acts on (including requests whose loan dates pass while still 'Requested').
gaps.why_it_matters: Loans are date-bound, so a request left unactioned past its From date has no defined outcome. A decline with no visible reason leaves staff unable to act on it.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Requests may sit in 'Requested' indefinitely or after their dates, and decline data and display cannot be specified.

gaps.title: Reporting-line edge cases for approval routing
gaps.description: DEC-001 restricts approval to the requester's own line manager. Not stated: where the reporting line comes from, what happens when a requester has no line manager recorded or the manager is absent, and what happens to pending requests when a requester changes manager or a manager leaves.
gaps.why_it_matters: With only the direct manager allowed to decide and no delegate stated, any gap in reporting data leaves a staff member's request with nobody able to approve it.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Requests can become stuck or be routed to the wrong person after organisational changes.

gaps.title: Who can submit and see which requests is unstated
gaps.description: Not stated: whether every staff member may request equipment, whether the Request equipment link is ever hidden or disabled, whether My equipment loans shows only the signed-in user's loans, and what a manager can see of their reports' loans outside the decision step. Sign-in requirements for the feature are not stated either.

evidence_refs.locator: ambiguous_behaviours[SCR-003] 'Is the list limited to the current user's loans'

gaps.why_it_matters: Loan records tie named staff to equipment and dates. Visibility rules decide whether colleagues or managers outside the reporting line can see them.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Access rules may be too open (exposing other staff's loans) or too narrow (blocking managers from context they need).

gaps.title: Item availability and overlapping requests
gaps.description: CQ-002 (whether availability is checked for the chosen dates and what happens if the item is unavailable) has not been answered. Also not stated: what happens when two staff request the same item for overlapping dates and both are approved by different managers.

evidence_refs.locator: ambiguous_behaviours[SCR-005] 'What happens if the chosen item is unavailable'

gaps.why_it_matters: Approval runs per reporting line, so separate managers could approve conflicting loans of the same physical item without seeing each other's decisions.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Double-booked equipment, approved loans that cannot be fulfilled, and undefined error behaviour on the request form.
research_questions: What are the common approaches in resource-booking systems to preventing double-booking: checking availability at request time, at approval time, or holding a tentative reservation?
How do equipment-loan or asset-booking tools typically present unavailability for a chosen date range to the requester?

gaps.title: Request form validation rules and error display
gaps.description: No field on the Request equipment form has a visible required marker. Not stated: which fields are required, cross-field date rules (To before From, dates in the past), limits on loan length or advance booking (part of CQ-003), and where and how errors are shown. No validation state was captured.
gaps.why_it_matters: The form's only inputs are an item and a date range. Invalid ranges would produce loans that cannot be approved or fulfilled.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Invalid or open-ended requests reach managers, and error behaviour is decided ad hoc during build.
research_questions: What do WCAG 2.2 SC 3.3.1 Error Identification and SC 3.3.3 Error Suggestion require when a date-range field fails validation?
What error-message and error-summary patterns does the GOV.UK Design System recommend for date inputs and date ranges?

gaps.title: Editing or cancelling a submitted request
gaps.description: CQ-003 (whether staff can edit or cancel after submitting) has not been answered. The loans table shows no row actions in the capture. Also not stated: whether an edit to an already approved request needs fresh approval, and whether a cancellation needs confirmation.

evidence_refs.locator: ambiguous_behaviours[SCR-003] 'Can a row be opened, edited or cancelled?'

gaps.why_it_matters: Plans change before a loan starts. Without a defined path, staff and managers have no way to free up equipment or correct dates.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: The lifecycle and status model stay incomplete, and approvals could apply to request details that were later changed.

gaps.title: Empty, loading and error states of the loans list
gaps.description: Only the default state of My equipment loans (one row) was captured. What the screen shows when a user has no loans, while loading, or when loading fails is not shown in the capture. How the list is sorted or paged as loans build up is not stated.
gaps.checklist_item: Empty, loading, success and error states
gaps.why_it_matters: This list is the landing screen for first-time users (who will have no loans) and the only place REQ-003's status is visible.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: New users see a blank or confusing screen, and failures could be mistaken for having no loans.
research_questions: What do established design systems recommend showing in an empty state for a personal records list that has a primary create action?

gaps.title: Email notification scope and delivery failure
gaps.description: DEC-002 confirms staff get an email when a request is approved or declined. Not stated: whether managers are notified of new requests from their reports, what the email contains, and what happens if the email cannot be delivered.
gaps.why_it_matters: No manager screen was captured (GAP-001), so it is unclear how managers learn a request is waiting. Email is the only confirmed channel for telling staff about decisions.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Requests may wait unseen by managers, and staff may miss decisions if email fails silently.
research_questions: What are common practices for handling bounced or failed transactional emails in workflow applications (retry, fallback to in-app display, logging)?

gaps.title: Item catalogue source and specific asset assignment
gaps.description: The form's Item selector shows generic options (Laptop, Projector), while the loans table shows a specific asset ('Laptop L-221'). Not stated: where the item list comes from, who maintains it, and when and by whom a specific asset is assigned to a request of a generic type.

evidence_refs.locator: ambiguous_behaviours[SCR-005] 'Where do the Item options come from'

gaps.why_it_matters: If staff request a type but loans are tracked per asset, someone outside the captured staff and manager roles must assign the asset. That role and step are not described anywhere.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: The data model (type versus asset) and the role responsible for the catalogue and assignment cannot be specified.

gaps.title: Traceability of approval decisions
gaps.description: Not stated: whether approval and decline decisions, and any edits or cancellations, must be recorded with who acted and when, and who can view that record.
gaps.why_it_matters: Organisational equipment is released on a manager's approval. If equipment is lost or a decision is disputed, the record of who approved it matters.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Disputed or mistaken approvals cannot be traced.

gaps.title: Duplicate submission of the same request
gaps.description: Not stated: what happens if Submit request is activated twice, or the same item and dates are submitted again while a request is still pending.
gaps.why_it_matters: Because submission feedback is undefined (GAP-002), staff are more likely to resubmit, which would create duplicate requests for their manager.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Duplicate pending requests clutter manager decisions and could lead to the same item being approved twice.
research_questions: What are the standard techniques for preventing duplicate form submissions in web applications (for example idempotency keys or disabling the control during submission), and what are their trade-offs?

gaps.title: Accessibility of date inputs and the status table
gaps.description: The form uses date inputs with an mm/dd/yyyy placeholder, and status is shown as text in a table column. Not stated: keyboard and screen-reader requirements for date entry, accessible labelling of the table, and how status changes or submission results are announced.
gaps.why_it_matters: All staff are expected to use the request form, and date entry is a known problem area for keyboard and screen-reader users.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Some staff may be unable to submit requests or read their loan status.
research_questions: What are the known accessibility issues with native HTML date inputs across major browsers and screen readers, and what does WCAG 2.2 AA require for them?
Which WCAG 2.2 success criteria apply to a data table used to display status values?

gaps.title: Date format and time zone conventions
gaps.description: The form placeholder shows mm/dd/yyyy, while the loans table shows dates as '3 Mar' and '7 Mar' with no year. Not stated: which date format and locale apply, whether the year is shown, and whether a loan's From and To are whole days in a particular time zone.
gaps.why_it_matters: Loan dates drive availability and approval. Ambiguous formats (day/month order) or a missing year can lead to requests for the wrong dates.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Staff may enter or read the wrong dates, and loans that span a year end display ambiguously.
research_questions: What do established guidelines (for example the GOV.UK Design System or the W3C internationalisation guidance) recommend for displaying and entering dates unambiguously?

assumptions.text: The 'Requested' status shown in the mockup is the state of a request waiting for a line manager's decision.
assumptions.why: Needed to relate the single observed status to the approve/decline step in REQ-002.
assumptions.impact: If 'Requested' means something else, the status model gap (GAP-003) widens.
assumptions.to_confirm: Confirm that 'Requested' means awaiting manager decision.

assumptions.text: 'L-221' in 'Laptop L-221' is an identifier of a specific physical asset rather than part of the item type name.
assumptions.why: The gap about type-versus-asset assignment depends on this reading.
assumptions.impact: If it is only a type name, GAP-012 is limited to catalogue ownership.
assumptions.to_confirm: Confirm whether loans are tracked per specific asset.

proposed_status_changes.reason: No manager-facing screen or flow is shown in the capture, and the decline reason and unactioned-request behaviour are unanswered (GAP-001, GAP-004).
The set of statuses and their transitions is not defined. Only 'Requested' is observed and CQ-005 is unanswered (GAP-003).
The submission outcome, validation rules and availability behaviour are undefined (GAP-002, GAP-007, GAP-008).
